title: Data Center Demand Added $11.10 per MWh to PJM Wholesale Power Costs in Early 2026
summary:
PJM's independent market monitor estimated wholesale power costs reached $114.50 per megawatt-hour (MWh) during the first half of 2026, noting that costs would have been $103.40 per MWh without the impact of data center demand on capacity. While data center demand added $11.10 per MWh to the total, the monitor found that these capacity costs were only a minority driver of the overall increase in wholesale prices during the period.

The primary cause of the price surge was the cost of electricity itself, which rose 47.7% compared to the first half of 2025. The Energy Information Administration also linked 2026 wholesale price hikes in some regions to extreme weather, specifically a winter storm and summer heat. Separately, a report from the Washington Post stated that data centers accounted for 4% of utility rate increases over the previous five years.
